patients.label: Case: 67-year-old man with progressive dysphagia and a giant esophageal IgG4-related pseudotumor resected by ESD
attribution_limitations: The biopsy of the left iliac crest lesion is reported as adenocarcinoma only "favoring the lung as primary origin"; the lung mass itself was never sampled.
The source says the patient received chemotherapy without naming agents, dates, or the target tumor.

Dates of the endoscopy, neck CT, FDG-PET and biopsies at the two previous hospitals are not given; they are ordered only as "previously" before the presentation to the authors' hospital, not among themselves.

The source says the patient "did not receive any medication including corticosteroid therapy after the ESD procedure" and later that he received chemotherapy for the subsequently found adenocarcinoma. The first statement is made in the context of IgG4-RD treatment; the two are not reconciled by the source.

The source gives no order words linking the chemotherapy to the iliac crest biopsy or to the death, and the final IgG4-RD diagnosis is linked to the histology and serum IgG4 only by basis wording ("Based on"); these pairs are left unordered.
